thesis: Crypto strategy v1 (November 11, 2026). Prospective HOLD of $1,000 in cash; multiweek BTC-versus-cash allocation thesis, reviewed after next completed Coinbase UTC daily bar and daily thereafter. The default-branch state and ledger through November 22 show $1,000 cash, zero crypto positions, zero pending orders, no fills and all prior crypto decisions HOLD; today's inbox file was absent on preflight. At the latest common November 22 completed mark, cash portfolio equity $1,000 versus passive BTC benchmark $805.10421 (0.013163253566649371 BTC initiated at $75,969.06 on November 5). The $194.90 difference is entirely due to remaining unexposed through a sharp BTC decline, not proof of a successful predictive signal; November is partial, and there is no October portfolio period to review. November 22 completed Coinbase BTC/USD candle: open $60,086, close $61,163.01; 20-day SMA $69,327.3735 versus $73,443.897 five days earlier (declining); close 11.78% below average; five-day return -5.719112%. A positive completed candle after the November 21 bounce is insufficient to establish a durable reversal. November 23 reports, separate from completed bars, describe BTC trading above $61,000 intraday and recovering from a November 21 low around $55,000. Reuters November 23 discusses whether the long-run BTC investment case survives a major exchange hack; this is a legitimate broad-exposure countercase, not an entry signal. The Block reports about $1.79bn in US spot BTC ETF net outflows last week, third-party fund-flow figures not independently verified on-chain; CoinDesk November 23 describes persistent US-session selling and uncertain rebound durability. BTC offers liquid broad crypto exposure and strategy permits a 5–15% starter without a proven forecast, but a still-declining 20-day average, negative five-day return, uncertain demand and simulated round-trip costs favor cash today. Completed November 22 ETH $1,721.29, SOL $70.61, ADA $0.14458 and LINK $8.811 are available, but none has a sufficiently corroborated independent catalyst and cost-adjusted thesis to justify switching from cash/BTC; other eligible coins lack independently verified distinct evidence. No held position exists to test against an entry thesis or exit condition; SELL is impossible. Reconsider a $50–$150 BTC BUY if completed daily BTC closes regain the 20-day average with improving five-day momentum, or several completed bars establish stabilization alongside credible spot demand improvement; do not mistake a single intraday rally for a completed-bar signal. No strategy revision warranted.
